appr.text: APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 66 Chapter 687 MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 4043, entitled: "AN ACT in relation to authorizing the Bedford Hills Fire District to file an application for exemption from school taxes and real property taxes" APPROVED This bill would authorize the Bedford Hills Fire District to file an application for retroactive exemption from school taxes and real proper- ty taxes for the 2022-2023 assessment roll. This bill as originally drafted requires a technical fix due to the unique legal status of the Bedford Hills Fire District, which operates within a special district. As such, it is covered under a different section of the Real Property Tax Law ("RPTL") than was initially refer- enced in the bill. The provisions governing special districts differ from those applicable in the municipal fire districts. The technical correction is necessary for the Bedford…

sponsored.t: Permits political parties to perform certain functions without forming county committees
sponsored.sum: Permits political parties to designate or nominate candidates for positions to be filled by all the voters, and perform other functions without forming county committees.

sponsored.t: Relates to prevailing wage requirements applicable to brownfield remediation work performed under private contract
sponsored.sum: Relates to prevailing wage requirements applicable to brownfield remediation work performed under private contract as it relates to certain remediation activities, for sites that are seeking or have received a determination that the site is eligible for the tangible property credit component of the brownfield redevelopment tax credit, and the work is paid for in whole or in part by public funds.

veto.text: VETO MESSAGE - No. 114 TO THE SENATE: I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill: Senate Bill Number 5379, entitled: "AN ACT to amend the environmental conservation law and the labor law, in relation to prevailing wage requirements applicable to brownfield remediation work performed under private contract" NOT APPROVED This bill would require prevailing wage as a condition of entering into the brownfield cleanup program (BCP), a voluntary program that offers tax credits towards the remediation and development of contam- inated sites. The bill would authorize the Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) to terminate a BCP agreement for violations of the new labor provisions. The bill would require DEC to expand its oversight of brownfield remediation projects and would require enforcement of new prevailing wage requirements. It is crucial that communities…

sponsored.t: Requires utilities to notify property owners prior to beginning certain services
sponsored.sum: Requires utilities to notify property owners prior to beginning any non-emergency construction or other work that may interfere with a property owner's ability to use, or access such owner's property; requires notice to include, but not limited to, a description of the work to be performed, the expected duration of such work, the location of such work, any road closures or detours that may occur due to such work, any action that may directly and materially impact the use of such property, and the contact information for the utility performing such work; provides notice may include electronic communications, signage, and written materials; exempts cases where a natural or man-made disaster…

veto.text: VETO MESSAGE - No. 82 TO THE SENATE: I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill: Senate Bill Number 1848, entitled: "AN ACT to amend the public service law, in relation to requiring corporations and municipalities to notify property owners prior to beginning certain services" NOT APPROVED This bill would require utilities to provide notice to customers of any non-emergency work which the utility reasonably believes will directly and materially impact the use of residential, commercial, or other property, not more than 30 days in advance of the start of such work. While I agree with the goal of this bill to ensure notification, the provisions of this bill present challenges for implementation and could impede utility work that is necessary to maintain the reliability and safety of New York's energy distribution systems. The ambiguity in this bill allows for…

sponsored.t: Prohibits the application of pesticides to certain local freshwater wetlands
sponsored.sum: Prohibits the application of pesticides to certain local freshwater wetlands for local governments that have implemented a freshwater wetlands protection law; provides that any local law or ordinance adopted pursuant to this section shall take effect on the first day of January after it shall have been adopted.

veto.text: VETO MESSAGE - No. 92 TO THE SENATE: I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill: Senate Bill Number 5983-A, entitled: "AN ACT to amend the environmental conservation law, in relation to prohibiting the application of pesticides to certain local fresh- water wetlands" NOT APPROVED This bill would allow a local government that has implemented a fresh- water wetlands protection law or ordinance in accordance with Environ- mental Conservation Law Section 24-0501 to adopt a local law or ordi- nance to prohibit the application of pesticides to wetlands it regulates. This bill is similar to legislation I vetoed last year due to concerns that it would undermine the integrity of the Department of Environmental Conservation's pesticide program, which is based on extensive scientific review. Additionally, this bill as written would create confusion and could result in the…

sponsored.t: Provides a tax exemption on real property owned by active auxiliary police officers in local law enforcement agencies in certain counties
sponsored.sum: Provides a tax exemption on real property owned by active auxiliary police officers in local law enforcement agencies in certain counties having a population of more than three hundred thirty-eight thousand and less than three hundred forty thousand, determined in accordance with the latest federal decennial census.

sponsored.t: Relates to the assessment of solar or wind energy systems
sponsored.sum: Relates to additional considerations regarding the assessment of solar or wind energy systems through a discounted cash flow approach.

sponsored.t: Authorizes the commissioner of general services to transfer and convey certain unappropriated state land to The Arc Westchester New York
sponsored.sum: Authorizes the commissioner of general services to transfer and convey certain unappropriated state land to The Arc Westchester New York.

sponsored.t: Relates to reduction of air pollution from petroleum bulk storage facilities
sponsored.sum: Expands the options for shell color and roof color of petroleum bulk storage tanks to either white or beige/cream or which limits volatile emissions to the same or to a greater extent as a shell color and roof color of white or beige/cream as determined by the department of environmental conservation.

sponsored.t: Authorizes adjudication of traffic control signal indications in the village of Croton-on-Hudson
sponsored.sum: Establishes a demonstration program imposing monetary liability on the owner of a vehicle for failure of an operator thereof to comply with traffic-control indications in the village of Croton-on-Hudson; repeals authorization of such program December 31, 2030.

sponsored.t: Requires police officers to take temporary custody of firearms when responding to reports of family violence
sponsored.sum: Requires police officers to take temporary custody of firearms for not less than one hundred twenty hours when responding to reports of family violence.

sponsored.t: Authorizes the town of Patterson to impose a hotel and motel tax
sponsored.sum: Authorizes the town of Patterson, in the county of Putnam, to impose a hotel and motel tax.

sponsored.t: Dedicates a portion of the state highway system to John F. McArdle
sponsored.sum: Dedicates a portion of the state highway system constituting state route three hundred one from Belden Road to Gipsy Trail Road in the town of Carmel, county of Putman, to John F. McArdle.

sponsored.t: Waives the residency requirement for the office of commissioner of finance of the county of Putnam
sponsored.sum: Waives the residency requirement for the office of commissioner of finance of the county of Putnam.

sponsored.t: Waives the residency requirement for the office of Putnam county attorney
sponsored.sum: Waives the residency requirement for the office of Putnam county attorney.

sponsored.t: Clarifies provisions regarding the use of crossbows for hunting
sponsored.sum: Clarifies provisions regarding the use of crossbows for hunting, allowing the department of environmental conservation to allow the use of crossbows for the taking of big game in any area long bows are permitted.

sponsored.t: Relates to the effectiveness of the occupancy tax in the village of Briarcliff Manor
sponsored.sum: Extends the effectiveness of the occupancy tax in the village of Briarcliff Manor by two years.

sponsored.t: Extends the one percent increased county sales tax for Putnam county
sponsored.sum: Extends the one percent increased county sales tax for Putnam county for two years; requires one-ninth of such one percent increase in sales tax be allocated to towns and villages in such county.
sponsored.fis: None for the state, increased revenue for the county

sponsored.t: Extends provisions relating to the imposition of an occupancy tax on the village of Mount Kisco until September 1, 2027
sponsored.sum: Extends provisions relating to the imposition of an occupancy tax on the village of Mount Kisco until September 1, 2027.

sponsored.t: Provides reimbursement for enhanced septic system projects
sponsored.sum: Provides reimbursement for enhanced septic system projects and defines what qualifies as an enhanced septic system project.
sponsored.fis: This bill would have no budget implications to the State as funding levels would remain the same. This bill would increase reimbursement amounts on individual projects.

sponsored.t: Relates to the elections of officers in the fire department in the village of Croton-on-Hudson in the county of Westchester
sponsored.sum: Authorizes the date of elections of officers in the fire department in the village of Croton-on-Hudson in the county of Westchester to vary from other village fire elections.

sponsored.t: Authorizes the village of Croton-on-Hudson to impose a hotel and motel tax
sponsored.sum: Authorizes the village of Croton-on-Hudson, in the county of Westchester, to impose a hotel and motel tax.

sponsored.t: Relates to qualifications to hold the position of assistant village engineer in the village of Croton-on-Hudson
sponsored.sum: Permits the village of Croton-on-Hudson to allow the office of assistant village engineer of such village to be held by a person who is not a resident of such village, provided that such person resides within Westchester county or an adjoining county within the state of New York.

sponsored.t: Makes technical corrections relating to the title of the commissioner of veterans' services
sponsored.sum: Makes technical corrections relating to the title of the commissioner of veterans' services.

sponsored.t: Requires allergen labeling for prepackaged foods
sponsored.sum: Requires every food establishment to label all prepackaged food with a written notification on the package or on a label attached to the package identifying any ingredient with which a product is made that constitutes a major food allergen.

sponsored.t: Permits the village of Croton-on-Hudson, Westchester county, to lease certain sports field fences for advertisements
sponsored.sum: Permits the village of Croton-on-Hudson, Westchester county, to lease certain sports field fences for advertisements, with revenues to be used solely for the care of Dobbs Park, Duck Pond Park, Firefighters Memorial Field and David J. Manes Memorial Field.
sponsored.fis: Increased revenue for the village of Croton-of-Hudson.

sponsored.t: Relates to adjudications and owner liability for a violation of traffic-control signal indications in the city of Peekskill
sponsored.sum: Relates to adjudications and owner liability for a violation of traffic-control signal indications in the city of Peekskill.

sponsored.t: Dedicates a portion of the state highway system to Westchester Purple Heart Recipients
sponsored.sum: Dedicates a portion of the state and local highway system constituting route thirty-five to Westchester Purple Heart Recipients.

sponsored.t: Dedicates a portion of the state highway system to Jake Arcara
sponsored.sum: Dedicates a portion of the state highway system in the town of Yorktown, county of Westchester, to Jake Arcara.

sponsored.t: Extends the effectiveness of certain provisions of chapter 329 of the laws of 2009, relating to removing special powers granted to the society for the prevention of cruelty to children
sponsored.sum: Relates to removing special powers granted to the society for the prevention of cruelty to children.

sponsored.t: Relates to the effectiveness of a presumption relating to certain lung disabilities incurred by volunteer firefighters
sponsored.sum: Amends provisions relating to creating a presumption relating to certain lung disabilities incurred by volunteer firefighters, in relation to the effectiveness of such provisions.

sponsored.t: Amends chapter 668 of the laws of 1977, amending the volunteer firefighters' benefit law relating to disability due to disease or malfunction of the heart or coronary arteries, in relation to the effectiveness
sponsored.sum: Extends the effectiveness of provisions relating to disability due to disease or malfunction of the heart or coronary arteries.

sponsored.t: Extends provisions relating to the establishment of the mercury thermostat collection act
sponsored.sum: Extends provisions relating to the establishment of the mercury thermostat collection act to January 1, 2027.

sponsored.t: Relates to the Mount Van Hoevenberg Olympic Sports Complex in Essex County
sponsored.sum: Relates to the Mount Van Hoevenberg Olympic Sports Complex in Essex County.
sponsored.fis: None, although the economy of the Lake Placid area and the State as a whole will benefit from the amendment.

sponsored.t: Relates to the Mount Van Hoevenberg Olympic Sports Complex in Essex County
sponsored.sum: Relates to the Mount Van Hoevenberg Olympic Sports Complex in Essex County.
sponsored.fis: None, although the economy of the Lake Placid area and the State as a whole will be benefited by the amendment.

sponsored.t: Protects the health insurance benefits of retirees of public employers and contributions of Medicare-eligible retirees of public employers
sponsored.sum: Prohibits public employers from diminishing health insurance benefits provided to Medicare-eligible retirees and their Medicare-eligible dependents or the contributions such employer makes for such health insurance coverage below the level of such benefits or contributions made on behalf of such retirees and dependents by the public employer as of December 31, 2021.

sponsored.t: Extends provisions of law relating to expanding the food donation and food scraps recycling program
sponsored.sum: Extends provisions of law relating to expanding the food donation and food scraps recycling program; amends the effectiveness relating thereto.

sponsored.t: Relates to the commissioner of corrections and community supervision's heat mitigation plan for correctional facilities
sponsored.sum: Relates to the commissioner of corrections and community supervision's heat mitigation plan for correctional facilities; provides findings regarding permanent cooling solutions shall be included.

sponsored.t: Defines medically fragile young adults for certain purposes
sponsored.sum: Defines medically fragile young adults as individuals who meet the definition of children with medical fragility, but for the fact such individuals are aged between twenty-one and thirty-five years old.
